about: A fast grammar checker that runs offline and keeps your writing private.

prs.title: No more false alarm on "the help they received"
prs.broken: Harper told people to change "they" to "them" in normal sentences like "the help they received" or "the support they needed".
prs.changed: When "they" is followed by a verb, so it is clearly the subject, the check now leaves it alone.
prs.matters: Fewer wrong warnings on everyday sentences, so people trust the real ones.

prs.title: "later" and "further" no longer flagged as wrong words
prs.broken: Harper only knew "later" and "further" as adjectives, so sentences like "She would later become president" got false grammar warnings.
prs.changed: Both words are now also marked as adverbs in the dictionary, which turns those two warnings off.
prs.matters: Writers stop seeing wrong corrections on two very common words.
